title: Sarah Martinez — Clothes Shopping Experience (Return Path)
summary: Sarah receives a promotional notification about a flash sale during her lunch break, finds an emerald green wrap dress, purchases it confidently thanks to the free returns policy, but returns it when it doesn't fit. Despite the return, the smooth process means she'd shop with StyleMart again. This experience follows the return path through the Online Clothes Shopping mission.

lanes.description: How this step causes pain for this actor — the gap between need and what the service provides

laneContent.thoughts: Oh, StyleMart has a flash sale... 40% off? That's actually good. Maybe I could get that cardigan I've been eyeing.

momentThatMatters.description: The notification arrives at a moment when Sarah can actually engage with it

laneContent.thoughts: Let me just have a quick look while I have a few minutes. The sale ends tonight so I need to decide soon.

actions: Filters by size and price range
laneContent.thoughts: There's so much here. Let me filter this down. I don't need another basic t-shirt... I want something a bit special that I wouldn't normally buy.

barriers.description: Difficult to assess fabric quality from photos alone
barriers.emergesFrom: Sarah's quality-conscious nature meets the limitations of digital shopping

opportunities: Add 'treat yourself' or 'special occasion' filter category

actions: Spots a wrap dress in a color she loves
Checks original price vs sale price
laneContent.thoughts: Oh this is lovely! That emerald green would be perfect for date nights. £85 down to £51... that's actually reasonable for a treat. I'd never pay full price but this feels justified.

momentThatMatters.description: Finding an item that feels special enough to be a treat but practical enough to justify

laneContent.thoughts: I'm usually a 10 but this brand might run small. The size guide says 10 is 28-inch waist... I think that's me? Maybe I should go for 12 to be safe. But then it might be too loose on top.
laneContent.needAtStep: Confidence that the size she picks will fit her body shape — not just measurements, but guidance on how this specific garment will sit on someone like her
laneContent.painAtStep: The size guide gives her numbers but not the answer she actually needs. Her analytical nature demands certainty, but the information provided creates more doubt, not less. She's forced to gamble on fit.

barriers.description: Size guide shows measurements but no guidance on fit style
barriers.emergesFrom: Sarah's anxiety about wrong decisions meets inadequate product information

actions: Filters to show reviews with photos
laneContent.thoughts: 4.2 stars from 89 reviews, that's decent. Let me see what people say about the fit... everyone says something different.
laneContent.needAtStep: Quick social validation from people like her — someone with a similar body type who bought this item and can confirm it works
laneContent.painAtStep: Her trust-but-verify approach is thwarted by contradictory reviews. She can't find the 'someone like me' signal in the noise, and her limited time means she can't read enough reviews to build statistical confidence.

barriers.emergesFrom: Sarah's analytical research style meets inconsistent user-generated content

momentThatMatters.description: Reading reviews that either build or undermine confidence in the purchase

laneContent.thoughts: Free returns within 30 days, that's reassuring. As long as I keep the tags on I can send it back if it doesn't fit. That makes this less risky.
I'll go with my usual size. If it doesn't fit, I can always return it.

actions: Checks that sale price is applied
Decides not to add more items
laneContent.thoughts: £51 total, free delivery over £50 — perfect, just made it. I don't need anything else, let's not get carried away.
Good, my address is saved. Standard delivery is fine, I'm not in a rush. Should arrive by Friday.
Love that I can just use Face ID. So much easier than typing card details.

actions: Closes app and returns to lunch
laneContent.thoughts: Done! That was quick. Excited for it to arrive. I deserve a little treat.

momentThatMatters.description: The moment of commitment — order placed, anticipation begins

actions: Receives push notification that order has shipped
laneContent.thoughts: Great, it's on its way. Should be here Thursday. Looking forward to trying it on.

actions: Opens app to check tracking status
Confirms still on track for Thursday
laneContent.thoughts: Just checking it's still coming tomorrow. Good, it's at the local depot.
The packaging is nice. Oh, the color is gorgeous, just like the photos. Fabric feels decent quality. Let me keep the tags on until I've tried it properly.

momentThatMatters.description: The unboxing experience — first physical interaction with the product

laneContent.thoughts: Hmm. The color is beautiful but... it's tight across the hips and the waist isn't sitting right. The wrap isn't falling properly. Maybe if I... no, it's just not the right fit for my body shape.
laneContent.needAtStep: To look and feel good in the dress — not just 'does it fit' but 'does it make me feel like the person I wanted to be when I bought it'
laneContent.painAtStep: The gap between the excitement of finding the dress and the reality of it not working on her body. She did everything right — researched, checked sizing, read reviews — and it still didn't work. This reinforces her anxiety that online shopping is fundamentally unreliable for clothes, despite the convenience she needs.

barriers.description: Sizing information didn't adequately predict fit for her body type
barriers.emergesFrom: Sarah's thorough research couldn't overcome the inherent limitations of online clothing shopping

opportunities: Virtual try-on using her body measurements
Size recommendation based on return history
Exchange flow that reserves the right size immediately

momentThatMatters.description: The critical moment of trying on and seeing yourself in the mirror

actions: Considers whether to keep it anyway
Checks if different size is available
laneContent.thoughts: Such a shame, I really love the color. Size 12 might have worked but it's sold out now. I can't keep something that doesn't fit properly — it'll just hang in my wardrobe. Better to return it and get my money back.

barriers.description: Preferred size is out of stock
barriers.emergesFrom: No exchange option available due to stock limitations

opportunities: Offer waitlist for size to become available
Suggest similar styles that might fit better
Provide exchange incentive to maintain the sale

actions: Opens app and goes to Orders
Finds the order and taps 'Return items'
laneContent.thoughts: Okay, let's get this return started. At least the app has a clear return option.

actions: Sees options: Post Office, Locker, Home collection
Chooses locker location near her office
laneContent.thoughts: Good, I can drop it at the locker near work. That's easy — I'll do it tomorrow on my lunch break.
Glad I kept the packaging. This is much easier than the old days of having to print labels.

actions: Goes to locker location during lunch
Opens app to display QR code
laneContent.thoughts: That was painless. Scanned, deposited, done. Should get my refund in a few days.

actions: Receives notification that return is being processed
laneContent.thoughts: Good, they've got it. Now I just need to wait for the refund.
Refund's come through. That was fairly painless overall. Shame the dress didn't fit but at least returning it wasn't a hassle. I'd still shop with them again.

momentThatMatters.description: Receiving the refund closes the loop and determines future purchase confidence

outcome.reflection: Despite the item not fitting, the overall experience was positive due to easy returns. Sarah would shop with StyleMart again. The key failure point was sizing prediction, not the service itself.
